summary: This Wikipedia article excerpt covers Muammar Gaddafi's rule of Libya, from his 1969 coup and the 1977 creation of the Jamahiriya to his later privatization reforms and death in 2011. It describes his ideology, which shifted from Arab nationalism and socialism toward his Third International Theory, Pan-Africanism, and anti-Zionism, along with his foreign relations with the US, the Soviet Union, Egypt, Italy and NATO. It also covers domestic institutions such as the Basic People's Congresses and the General People's Committees, and the final months of his rule during the 2011 uprising.
one_line: Overview of Muammar Gaddafi's rule over Libya, his ideology, foreign conflicts, economic reforms, and death in 2011.
key_facts: Gaddafi came to power in a bloodless coup in 1969 that seized power from the absolute monarchy of King Idris.

On 2 March 1977 the General People's Congress adopted the "Declaration of the Establishment of the People's Authority", replacing the Libyan Arab Republic with the Great Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya.
The Jamahiriya was officially a direct democracy operating through 187 Basic People's Congresses.
In 1973 Gaddafi initiated a "Popular Revolution" with the formation of General People's Committees, and outlined his Third International Theory that year in The Green Book.
In October 1969 Gaddafi proclaimed the trade terms for Libyan oil unfair, and in December Jalloud successfully increased the price of Libyan oil.
In 1970 other OPEC states followed suit, leading to a global increase in the price of crude oil.
In October 1970 all Italian-owned assets were expropriated and the 12,000-strong Italian community was expelled from Libya.
In 1981 US President Ronald Reagan erroneously considered Libya a puppet regime of the Soviet Union, and in March 1982 the U.S. implemented an embargo of Libyan oil.
In April 1984 Libyan diplomats were accused in the shooting death of British policewoman Yvonne Fletcher outside the London embassy, breaking down diplomatic relations with the U.K.
In 2007 Gaddafi advocated the Isratin single-state solution to the Israeli–Palestinian conflict.
By 2004 there was $40 billion of direct foreign investment in Libya, a sixfold rise over 2003.
In October 2010 Gaddafi apologized to African leaders on behalf of Arab nations for their involvement in the African slave trade.
On 20 October Gaddafi broke out of Sirte's District 2 in a convoy, and NATO bombers attacked, killing at least 53.
On 30 April a NATO airstrike killed Gaddafi's sixth son and three of his grandsons in Tripoli, though Gaddafi and his wife were unharmed.
In December 1978 Gaddafi stepped down as Secretary-General of the GPC and adopted the title "Leader of the Revolution".

entities.name: Muammar Muhammad Abu Minyar al-Gaddafi
entities.role: Libyan revolutionary, politician and political theorist who governed Libya from 1969 to 2011, subject of the article

entities.name: King Idris
entities.role: pro-western monarch of the United Kingdom of Libya whose absolute monarchy was overthrown in the 1969 coup

entities.name: Gamal Abdel Nasser
entities.role: Egyptian president and Gaddafi's hero, whose book Philosophy of the Revolution was a key influence

entities.name: Anwar Sadat
entities.role: successor to Nasser who proposed a political federation with Libya and signed an unofficial charter of merger with Gaddafi in 1972

entities.name: Ronald Reagan
entities.role: US President who pursued a hard-line approach to Libya from 1981

entities.name: Yvonne Fletcher
entities.role: British policewoman shot dead outside Libya's London embassy in April 1984

entities.name: Saif al-Islam Gaddafi
entities.role: Gaddafi's son and heir apparent, a reformist who was openly critical of Libya's human rights record

entities.name: Abu-Bakr Yunis Jabr
entities.role: Libyan defence minister killed in the conflict at Sirte in October 2011

entities.name: Jalloud
entities.role: official who successfully increased the price of Libyan oil in December 1969

entities.name: Robert Gates
entities.role: U.S. Secretary of Defense who said NATO was not targeting Gaddafi specifically

entities.name: Blundy and Lycett
entities.role: authors who described Gaddafi's anti-Semitism as almost Hitlerian

entities.name: Abdessalam Bouminyar
entities.role: Gaddafi's paternal grandfather, who according to later claims was killed by the Italian Army during the 1911 invasion

entities.name: Revolutionary Command Council (RCC)
entities.role: governing body after the 1969 coup, of which Gaddafi became Chairman

entities.name: General People's Congress
entities.role: annual body of delegates from the Basic People's Congresses, broadcast live on television, and adopted the 1977 declaration

entities.name: General People's Committees (GPCs)
entities.role: local working groups formed in 1973 as a purported system of direct democracy, also serving as a surveillance system

entities.name: National Transitional Council (NTC)
entities.role: rebel body that rejected Gaddafi's suggestion of a negotiated handover to a transitional government

entities.name: NATO
entities.role: alliance whose bombers attacked Gaddafi's convoy and whose airstrikes killed his sixth son and grandsons

entities.name: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)
entities.role: oil cartel whose other states followed Libya in raising oil prices in 1970

entities.name: Voice of the Arabs
entities.role: Cairo-based pan-Arab radio broadcast that Gaddafi listened to while growing up

entities.name: The Green Book
entities.role: publication in which Gaddafi outlined his Third International Theory in 1973

entities.name: Philosophy of the Revolution
entities.role: book by Nasser, described as the inspiration and blueprint of Gaddafi's revolution

entities.name: Jamahiriya
entities.role: Great Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya, the state of the masses conceptualized by Gaddafi from 1977

entities.name: Sirte
entities.role: city to which Gaddafi retreated after Tripoli's fall and where he was killed

entities.name: Sabha
entities.role: town where Gaddafi became involved in politics while at school

entities.name: Gulf of Sirte
entities.role: sea area Libya claimed as territorial waters, where US forces shot down two Libyan planes in 1981

entities.name: Tripoli
entities.role: Libyan capital, site of the NATO airstrike that killed Gaddafi's son and grandsons

entities.name: Malta
entities.role: island whose government was asked by Libya in 1971 to stop allowing NATO use of its land for a base

entities.name: Misrata
entities.role: city whose rebel militia shelled the villa where Gaddafi and his cohort fled
